title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
authors: Ali Behrouz, Peilin Zhong, Vahab Mirrokni (Google Research)
tldr: Titans introduces a deep neural long-term memory module (LMM): an MLP whose weights are updated at test time by gradient descent with data-dependent momentum and weight decay on an associative-memory (key-to-value regression) loss, so the gradient magnitude acts as a 'surprise' signal deciding what gets memorized. The recurrence M_t = (1-alpha_t) M_{t-1} + S_t, S_t = eta_t S_{t-1} - theta_t grad(loss), strictly generalizes Gated DeltaNet, Longhorn, RWKV-7, and TTT layers (which are recovered as special cases), while allowing a deep nonlinear memory instead of a matrix state. Training is made parallel via chunkwise mini-batch gradient descent: within a chunk, gradients are taken at the chunk-start weights so everything tensorizes into matmuls, and the momentum recurrence is computed with a parallel associative scan. Three hybrid architectures (Memory as Context / Gate / Layer) combine this long-term memory with windowed attention (short-term memory) and learnable data-independent 'persistent memory' tokens. At 340M-760M parameters on 15-30B tokens, Titans beats Transformer++, Mamba/Mamba2, DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet, TTT and hybrid baselines on language modeling and commonsense reasoning, holds ~95-98% accuracy on RULER S-NIAH out to 16K where Mamba2 collapses, and the MAC variant scales past 2M context on BABILong, outperforming GPT-4 and Llama3.1-8B+RAG with roughly 70x fewer parameters.
problem_and_motivation: Attention gives exact pairwise dependency modeling but costs O(N^2) time and memory in context length N, capping usable context; the KV cache is a memory that grows without compression. Linear Transformers / linear RNNs / SSMs fix the cost by compressing history into a fixed-size vector- or matrix-valued state, but the paper points out a contradiction: the regimes where linear cost matters most (very long context) are exactly where a small linear state cannot faithfully compress the history, so linear models underperform. The paper reframes all sequence models through a memory lens: a model has a memory structure, a write (update) rule, and a read (retrieval) rule. Transformers append uncompressed KV pairs (growing memory, exact reads); linear attention additively writes k v^T outer products into one matrix (overflow-prone); gated variants (GLA, Mamba2, Griffin, xLSTM) add data-dependent erasure; delta-rule variants (DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet) replace-then-write. Five design questions are posed: (Q1) what memory structure, (Q2) what update rule, (Q3) what retrieval rule, (Q4) how to compose multiple interconnected memory systems (mirroring human short-term/long-term/meta memory), and (Q5) whether memory must be DEEP (nonlinear, multi-layer) rather than a single matrix that can only fit history to a linear map. The proposed answer: a deep MLP memory trained online at test time by an inner gradient-descent loop with momentum ('past surprise') and weight decay ('forgetting'), composed with attention as short-term memory and learnable static tokens as persistent (task) memory. A secondary motivation is that memorizing training data is undesirable (generalization, privacy, OOD test data), so the model should meta-learn HOW to memorize, and do the actual memorization only at test time on the test context. NOTE FOR INFERENCE-ONLY READERS: 'training at test time' here means running an optimizer over a small module's weights during the forward pass of inference; the paper's whole contribution is making that inner optimization expressive (momentum, decay, depth) yet parallelizable.
core_mechanism:
MEMORY AS A MODULE'S WEIGHTS. The long-term memory M is a small neural network (in this paper an MLP with $L_{\mathcal{M}} \ge 1$ layers, input/output width $d_{in}$). Its weights ARE the recurrent state. Notation: $\mathcal{M}(x)$ is a forward pass that also triggers a weight update (a write); $\mathcal{M}^*(x)$ is a forward pass WITHOUT weight adjustment (a read); subscript $t$ indexes the state over time.

KEYS/VALUES/QUERIES OF THE INNER PROBLEM. Each token $x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{in}}$ is projected by outer-loop-learned matrices: $\mathbf{k}_t = x_t W_K$, $\mathbf{v}_t = x_t W_V$, $\mathbf{q}_t = x_t W_Q$ with $W_K, W_V, W_Q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{in} \times d_{in}}$. Crucially these are 'hyperparameters' of the inner loss (fixed during inference), trained only in the outer loop.

INNER OBJECTIVE (what the memory learns at test time). Associative-memory regression: $\ell(\mathcal{M}_{t-1}; x_t) = \| \mathcal{M}_{t-1}(\mathbf{k}_t) - \mathbf{v}_t \|_2^2$. Rationale: memory should store key-to-value mappings so that later, given a query similar to a stored key, it returns the associated value — same abstraction as attention's KV lookup, but stored in weights. If $\mathcal{M}$ is a single matrix $W \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times d_{in}}$ this is exactly online LINEAR regression, i.e., it presumes history is linearly compressible — the paper's argument for depth ($L_{\mathcal{M}} \ge 2$): an MLP memory can store nonlinear key-value structure (backed by universal-approximation reasoning and by the deep-memory ablation).

SURPRISE METRIC AND BASE UPDATE (Eq. 8): $\mathcal{M}_t = \mathcal{M}_{t-1} - \theta_t \nabla \ell(\mathcal{M}_{t-1}; x_t)$. The gradient of the memory's loss w.r.t. its weights measures how badly the current token violates what is already stored — the paper's operational definition of 'momentary surprise' (large gradient = novel/unexpected = worth memorizing hard). $\theta_t$ is a data-dependent inner learning rate (a function of $x_t$).

MOMENTUM = MEMORY OF SURPRISE (Eqs. 9-10). Pure momentary surprise fails: after a surprise spike, gradients shrink and the model may under-memorize the important tokens that FOLLOW a surprising event (the paper's analogy: the surprising moment grabs attention for a whole time frame). So surprise is decomposed into past + momentary: $\mathcal{M}_t = \mathcal{M}_{t-1} + S_t$, $S_t = \eta_t S_{t-1} - \theta_t \nabla \ell(\mathcal{M}_{t-1}; x_t)$, where $S_t$ (same shape as the weights) is 'past surprise' and is literally the momentum buffer of SGD-with-momentum; $\eta_t \in [0,1]$ is a DATA-DEPENDENT surprise decay: $\eta_t \to 0$ cuts the surprise carryover (context switch), $\eta_t \to 1$ fully propagates it (token strongly tied to recent context). Making $\eta_t, \theta_t$ functions of $x_t$ is emphasized as essential: whether past surprise should influence the current write depends on whether tokens share a context.

FORGETTING GATE = WEIGHT DECAY (Eqs. 13-14, the final update rule): $\mathcal{M}_t = (1 - \alpha_t)\, \mathcal{M}_{t-1} + S_t$, $S_t = \eta_t S_{t-1} - \theta_t \nabla \ell(\mathcal{M}_{t-1}; x_t)$, with data-dependent $\alpha_t \in [0,1]$: $\alpha_t \to 0$ preserves the whole past abstraction, $\alpha_t \to 1$ wipes the memory. This is exactly weight decay applied per token, and the paper shows it generalizes the gating/forgetting of modern linear RNNs (Mamba2, GLA, Gated DeltaNet). Net effect: the whole memory write is one step of MINI-BATCH GRADIENT DESCENT WITH MOMENTUM AND WEIGHT DECAY, with all three optimizer scalars gated per token. Ablations rank contributions: weight decay > momentum > convolution > persistent memory.

RETRIEVAL (Eq. 15): $y_t = \mathcal{M}^*(\mathbf{q}_t)$ — an inference-only forward pass through the memory MLP with the query projection; no weight change on read.

PERSISTENT MEMORY (Sec. 3.3). A set of $N_p \ge 1$ learnable, input-INdependent vectors $P = [p_1 \ldots p_{N_p}]$ prepended to the sequence: $x_{new} = P \,\|\, x$. Three justifications: (1) memory-systems view — task knowledge ('how to do the task') should live in parameters that do not change with input, complementing the contextual LMM; (2) FFN view — Sukhbaatar et al. showed $FFN(x) = W_V\, \mathrm{Softmax}(W_K x)$ is attention with data-independent K/V, so persistent tokens play the same role inside attention; (3) technical view — causal attention over-weights initial tokens (attention-sink effect), and learnable prefix tokens absorb/redistribute that bias.

THE THREE TITANS COMPOSITIONS (Sec. 4). All treat attention as precise SHORT-TERM memory and the LMM as fading LONG-TERM memory, plus persistent tokens.
(a) MEMORY AS CONTEXT (MAC): chunk the sequence into segments $S^{(i)}$ of fixed size $C$. For incoming segment $S^{(t)}$: retrieve history $h_t = \mathcal{M}^*_{t-1}(\mathbf{q}_t)$ with $\mathbf{q}_t = S^{(t)} W_Q$ (segment tokens query the memory); form the augmented segment $\tilde{S}^{(t)} = [p_1 \ldots p_{N_p}] \,\|\, h_t \,\|\, S^{(t)}$; run FULL causal attention within it, $y_t = \mathrm{Attn}(\tilde{S}^{(t)})$; then WRITE the attention output into memory, $\mathcal{M}_t = \mathcal{M}_{t-1}(y_t)$ (i.e., run the inner-loop update over the tokens of $y_t$), and output $o_t = y_t \otimes \mathcal{M}^*_t(y_t)$. Design rationale: attention sees both retrieved history and current data, so it (i) decides per token whether long-term memory is even needed, and (ii) FILTERS what enters long-term memory — only attention-processed representations are written, mitigating memory overflow from useless tokens. At test time: persistent params frozen, attention weights act as the in-context learner, LMM weights keep updating.
(b) MEMORY AS GATE (MAG): no segmentation. $\tilde{x} = P \,\|\, x$; branch 1: $y = \text{SW-Attn}^*(\tilde{x})$ (sliding-window attention WITH the persistent prefix always visible); branch 2: the LMM recurs over the whole sequence; combine $o = y \otimes \mathcal{M}(\tilde{x})$ where $\otimes$ is a nonlinear gate — in experiments, each branch output is normalized with learnable vector-valued weights, passed through a nonlinearity $\sigma(\cdot)$, and multiplied. SWA = sharp short-term memory, LMM = fading long-term memory; interpretable as a multi-head layer whose heads have heterogeneous structure (as in Hymba).
(c) MEMORY AS LAYER (MAL): $\tilde{x} = P \,\|\, x$; $y = \mathcal{M}(\tilde{x})$; $o = \text{SW-Attn}(y)$ — the conventional stacked-hybrid pattern (H3-style, with the LMM replacing the SSM). Explicitly identified as the WEAKEST composition because the pipeline is bottlenecked by each stage; included because virtually all existing hybrids (Samba, Griffin, H3, etc.) are MAL-shaped.
(d) LMM alone: the memory used as a standalone sequence model with no attention, to test that long-term memory is powerful even in isolation.

BLOCK DETAILS (Sec. 4.4): residual connections everywhere; SiLU activation when computing q/k/v; $\ell_2$-normalization of queries and keys; a 1D depthwise-separable convolution after each of the q, k, v projections (small but positive effect, cheap); normalization + linear-layer gating before the final output projection.

EXPRESSIVITY (Theorem 4.1): Transformers, diagonal linear RNNs, and DeltaNet are confined to complexity class $TC^0$ (Merrill et al.), but Titans are claimed to solve problems beyond $TC^0$, i.e., strictly more expressive for state tracking. The extra power comes from the nonlinear (deep-memory, inter-chunk) recurrence. (No proof appears in the v1 text.)

LINEAR-MEMORY SPECIAL CASE (Appendix C, the bridge to prior art). With $\mathcal{M}_t = W_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times d_{in}}$ and $\ell = \frac{1}{2}\|\mathcal{M}_t \mathbf{k}_t - \mathbf{v}_t\|_2^2$, the update becomes $\mathcal{M}_t = \mathrm{diag}(1-\alpha_t)\mathcal{M}_{t-1} + S_t$, $S_t = \mathrm{diag}(\eta_t) S_{t-1} - \mathrm{diag}(\theta_t)\big(\mathcal{M}_{t-1}\mathbf{k}_t^{\top}\mathbf{k}_t - \mathbf{v}_t^{\top}\mathbf{k}_t\big)$. Setting $\eta_t = 0$ recovers Gated DeltaNet's rule $S_{t+1} = S_t (I - \theta_t \mathbf{k}_t \mathbf{k}_t^{\top}) + \theta_t \mathbf{v}_t \mathbf{k}_t^{\top}$ (with decay); Longhorn is the same delta form with implicit-online-learning step size $\delta_t = \theta_t / (1 + \theta_t \mathbf{k}_t^{\top} \mathbf{k}_t)$ but NO forget gate; RWKV-7 uses the same loss/formulation; TTT is the gradient-based special case without forgetting and without momentum. So the LMM generalizes this whole family along four axes: momentum-based (token-flow-aware) updates, deep memory, nonlinear (inter-chunk) recurrence, and a forget gate.
outer_loop_training:
WHAT IS META-LEARNED. Everything except the memory's transient state: the inner-problem projections $W_K, W_V, W_Q$ (which define WHAT the memory is asked to store and how it is queried), the networks producing the per-token optimizer gates $\alpha_t, \theta_t, \eta_t$ (parameterization not spelled out in v1; by convention these are linear heads + sigmoid on $x_t$), the persistent-memory tokens $P$, the attention blocks, the depthwise-separable convolutions, output gates/normalizations, embeddings/LM head, and implicitly the initialization $\mathcal{M}_0$ of the memory weights. The paper frames this explicitly as meta-learning: 'training of the memory is in the inner loop, so $W_K$ and $W_V$ are hyperparameters of the inner loss; in the inner loop we optimize $\mathcal{M}$'s weights, in the outer loop we optimize the rest of the architecture' (citing Reptile/CAVIA-style meta-learning). The outer objective is ordinary next-token cross-entropy; gradients flow through the unrolled inner-loop updates by automatic differentiation — i.e., the chunkwise closed forms below ARE the forward graph that autodiff backprops through. BACKGROUND SCAFFOLDING NEEDED for inference-focused readers: (1) gradient descent / momentum / weight decay as an update recurrence, (2) the inner/outer-loop (bilevel) structure of meta-learning and what 'differentiating through an optimizer' means, (3) parallel associative scan (the same primitive as in S5/Mamba).

CHUNKWISE-PARALLEL FORMULATION (Sec. 3.2, the trick that makes pre-training feasible). Naively the inner loop is a strictly sequential per-token weight update — O(N) FLOPs but zero parallelism and no matmuls. Following TTT (Sun et al. 2024), the sequence is split into chunks of size $b$, and within a chunk all gradients are evaluated at the CHUNK-START weights (mini-batch instead of pure online GD): with $t' = t - \mathrm{mod}(t, b)$ and $\beta_i = \prod_{j=1}^{i}(1-\alpha_j)$, the decay-plus-gradient recurrence unrolls to the closed form $\mathcal{M}_t = \beta_t \mathcal{M}_0 - \sum_{i=1}^{t} \theta_i \frac{\beta_t}{\beta_i} \nabla \ell(\mathcal{M}_{t'}; x_i)$. Because every gradient in a chunk uses the same frozen weights $\mathcal{M}_{t'}$, all $b$ gradients are computable simultaneously as one batched matmul. For the linear-memory case: $\nabla \ell(W_0; x_t) = (W_0 x_t - x_t) x_t^{\top}$ (paper's shorthand; with the associative loss the literal form is $(W_0 \mathbf{k}_t - \mathbf{v}_t)\mathbf{k}_t^{\top}$), giving the tensorized chunk expression $\sum_{i=1}^{b} \theta_i \frac{\beta_b}{\beta_i} \nabla \ell(W_0; x_i) = \Theta_b \mathbf{B}_b (W_0 X - X) X^{\top}$, where $\Theta_b = \mathrm{diag}(\theta_1, \ldots, \theta_b)$ and $\mathbf{B}_b$ is the analogous diagonal of decay ratios $\beta_b / \beta_i$; only per-chunk $\Theta, \mathbf{B}$ need be stored, not all $N/b$ of them at once. The MLP case ($L_{\mathcal{M}} \ge 2$) 'is similar' — per-layer gradients at chunk-start weights, batched.

MOMENTUM VIA ASSOCIATIVE SCAN. Within a chunk, with $u_t = \nabla \ell(\mathcal{M}_{t'}; x_t)$ all precomputed in parallel, the momentum recurrence $S_t = \eta_t S_{t-1} - \theta_t u_t$ is a first-order LINEAR recurrence with input-dependent transition $\eta_t$, hidden state $S_t$, input $u_t$ — exactly the shape solved by a parallel (Blelloch-style) associative scan as in S5/Mamba, giving log-depth parallel computation of all $S_t$ in the chunk.

RESULTING RECURRENCE STRUCTURE: INTRA-CHUNK LINEAR, INTER-CHUNK NONLINEAR. Within a chunk everything is linear in the state (matmuls + scan); across chunk boundaries, the updated MLP weights re-enter the loss nonlinearly (the next chunk's gradients are taken at the new weights, through the MLP's nonlinearities). This hybrid is both the parallelization story and the claimed source of beyond-$TC^0$ expressivity — a deliberately different trade than DeltaNet/Gated DeltaNet, which stay fully linear to get exact closed-form chunkwise recurrences.

FURTHER SPEED OPTION — PARAMETERS AS FUNCTIONS OF CHUNKS: if $\alpha, \theta, \eta$ are made constant within each chunk (learnable but time-invariant per chunk) instead of per token, $\Theta$ collapses to a scalar and the momentum recurrence becomes a linear time-invariant (LTI) system computable with a GLOBAL CONVOLUTION (S4-style FFT conv). The experiments do NOT use this (they keep per-token gates for expressivity); it is flagged as future work for training larger models.

OUTER-LOOP RECIPE (Sec. 5.1): training length 4K tokens, Llama-2 tokenizer (32K vocab), AdamW, lr 4e-4, cosine annealing, batch 0.5M tokens, weight decay 0.1, following the Gated DeltaNet training protocol; 15B tokens of FineWeb-Edu for 170M/340M/400M models, 30B tokens for 760M. Training throughput scales linearly in sequence length (constant tokens/sec, Fig. 8), with a linear slowdown per extra memory layer $L_{\mathcal{M}}$.
inner_loop_test_time:
WHAT CHANGES DURING INFERENCE. Two tensors evolve per sequence: the memory weights $\mathcal{M}_t$ (all parameters of the $L_{\mathcal{M}}$-layer memory MLP) and the momentum buffer $S_t$ (same shape as $\mathcal{M}$). Everything else — $W_{Q/K/V}$, attention, persistent tokens $P$, gate heads, convs — is frozen at inference. The optimizer applied per token (or per attention-filtered token in MAC) is gradient descent with momentum and weight decay whose three scalars $\theta_t$ (step size), $\eta_t$ (momentum decay), $\alpha_t$ (weight decay) are emitted by learned gates from the current token: $S_t = \eta_t S_{t-1} - \theta_t \nabla_{\mathcal{M}} \| \mathcal{M}_{t-1}(\mathbf{k}_t) - \mathbf{v}_t \|_2^2$; $\mathcal{M}_t = (1-\alpha_t)\mathcal{M}_{t-1} + S_t$. Reads are plain forward passes $y_t = \mathcal{M}^*(\mathbf{q}_t)$.

PER-TOKEN COMPUTE. Let $P_{\mathcal{M}}$ be the memory parameter count (for width-$d$ MLP, $P_{\mathcal{M}} \approx L_{\mathcal{M}} d^2$; for the linear case, $d^2$). A write costs: 2 projections ($2d^2$ MACs for k,v) + 1 forward through $\mathcal{M}$ ($\approx P_{\mathcal{M}}$ MACs) + 1 backward through $\mathcal{M}$ to get the weight gradient ($\approx 2 P_{\mathcal{M}}$ MACs — the standard 2x-forward cost of backprop, which for the linear case degenerates to the rank-1 outer product $(W\mathbf{k}_t - \mathbf{v}_t)\mathbf{k}_t^{\top}$) + the elementwise state update ($\approx 2 P_{\mathcal{M}}$ multiply-adds over $S$ and $\mathcal{M}$) + three tiny gate evaluations. A read adds one projection + one forward ($\approx d^2 + P_{\mathcal{M}}$). Total $\approx 5$-$6 \times P_{\mathcal{M}}$ FLOP-equivalents per token — a constant independent of context length, i.e., a small constant factor over a linear-attention/DeltaNet layer of the same state size, with the factor growing linearly in memory depth $L_{\mathcal{M}}$ (empirically: LMM slightly slower than Mamba2/Gated DeltaNet, Fig. 8-9).

STATE SIZE. Per LMM layer per sequence: $2 P_{\mathcal{M}}$ numbers ($\mathcal{M}_t$ + $S_t$) — e.g., a 2-layer memory of width $d = 1024$ holds ~2M weights + ~2M momentum entries per head-group, per layer. This is larger than a Mamba2/DeltaNet matrix state ($d \times d_{state}$) but CONSTANT in N, versus a KV cache growing as $2 N d$ per layer: at 2M-token context the attention KV cache is out of reach while the LMM state is unchanged — this is precisely how Titans (MAC) runs >2M-token BABILong. In MAC, attention itself only ever sees one segment ($C$ tokens) plus $N_p$ persistent + retrieved-history tokens, so the attention KV cache is bounded by the segment size; in MAG/MAL the SWA window bounds it.

VARIANT-SPECIFIC INNER-LOOP FLOW. LMM/MAG/MAL update memory on every token of the (prefix-augmented) stream. MAC operates segment-at-a-time: read with the whole incoming segment as queries ($h_t = \mathcal{M}^*_{t-1}(S^{(t)} W_Q)$), attend over persistent + retrieved + current tokens, then write the ATTENTION OUTPUTS $y_t$ into the memory ($\mathcal{M}_t = \mathcal{M}_{t-1}(y_t)$) — attention acts as a learned write-filter deciding what deserves long-term storage. At test time the persistent parameters stay fixed (task knowledge), attention performs in-context learning within the window, and only the LMM 'is still learning'. Chunkwise (size-$b$) mini-batch semantics can be kept at inference for prefill (parallel ingest of a long prompt), while decode can proceed token-by-token; the outer-loop/inner-loop math is identical in both phases — there is no train/inference discrepancy in the update rule itself, only in whether outer gradients are also computed.

concepts_introduced.name: Neural long-term memory module (LMM)
concepts_introduced.definition: A deep MLP whose weights serve as the recurrent state of a sequence model and are updated at test time by an inner gradient-descent loop on an associative-memory loss; also usable standalone as a sequence model (Titans (LMM)).

concepts_introduced.name: Surprise metric (momentary surprise)
concepts_introduced.definition: The gradient of the memory's associative loss w.r.t. the memory weights, $\nabla \ell(\mathcal{M}_{t-1}; x_t)$; large gradient = input violates stored expectations = memorize more strongly.

concepts_introduced.name: Past surprise / momentum as surprise memory
concepts_introduced.definition: The momentum buffer $S_t = \eta_t S_{t-1} - \theta_t \nabla \ell$, interpreted as carrying surprise across tokens so that tokens following a surprising event are still memorized; claimed first momentum-based update rule in a linear-recurrent-style model.

concepts_introduced.name: Data-dependent surprise decay $\eta_t$
concepts_introduced.definition: Token-conditioned gate on the momentum term controlling whether past surprise propagates ($\eta_t \to 1$) or is cut at a context switch ($\eta_t \to 0$).

concepts_introduced.name: Forgetting mechanism as weight decay $\alpha_t$
concepts_introduced.definition: Per-token data-dependent weight decay $(1-\alpha_t)\mathcal{M}_{t-1}$, shown to generalize the forget/decay gates of Mamba2, GLA, and Gated DeltaNet to arbitrary (deep) memory.

concepts_introduced.name: Associative memory inner objective
concepts_introduced.definition: $\ell(\mathcal{M}; x_t) = \|\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{k}_t) - \mathbf{v}_t\|_2^2$ with outer-learned projections $W_K, W_V$ acting as hyperparameters of the inner problem.

concepts_introduced.name: Persistent memory
concepts_introduced.definition: $N_p$ learnable, input-independent tokens prepended to the sequence, storing task knowledge; motivated as data-independent attention K/V (FFN analogy) and as attention-sink absorbers. Term imported from Sukhbaatar et al. 2019 / Hymba's meta-tokens.

concepts_introduced.name: Contextual memory
concepts_introduced.definition: The paper's umbrella term for memory whose contents depend on the input context (the LMM and attention's KV), contrasted with persistent (input-independent) memory.

concepts_introduced.name: Memory as Context (MAC)
concepts_introduced.definition: Titans variant: segment the sequence; per segment, retrieve from the LMM, concatenate [persistent || retrieved || segment], run full attention within the window, write attention outputs back into the LMM; generalizes Recurrent Memory Transformer with a neural memory instead of a 16-dim vector.

concepts_introduced.name: Memory as Gate (MAG)
concepts_introduced.definition: Titans variant: sliding-window attention branch and LMM branch over the same (persistent-prefixed) sequence, combined by a learned elementwise gate.

concepts_introduced.name: Memory as Layer (MAL)
concepts_introduced.definition: Titans variant: LMM stacked sequentially before sliding-window attention (the conventional hybrid pattern, H3-style); identified as the least expressive composition.

concepts_introduced.name: $\mathcal{M}(x)$ vs $\mathcal{M}^*(x)$ notation
concepts_introduced.definition: Forward pass with weight adjustment (write) vs without (read); reads are pure inference through the memory MLP with the query projection.

concepts_introduced.name: Chunkwise mini-batch inner GD (parameters at chunk-start)
concepts_introduced.definition: Parallelization scheme (extending TTT): within a chunk of size $b$ all inner gradients are evaluated at the chunk-start weights $\mathcal{M}_{t'}$, $t' = t - \mathrm{mod}(t,b)$, tensorizing the update into matmuls $\Theta_b \mathbf{B}_b (W_0 X - X) X^{\top}$ plus an associative scan for momentum.

concepts_introduced.name: Intra-chunk linear / inter-chunk nonlinear recurrence
concepts_introduced.definition: The resulting hybrid recurrence class: linear (scan-parallel) inside chunks, nonlinear (through the MLP) across chunk boundaries; cited as the source of expressivity beyond $TC^0$ (Theorem 4.1).

concepts_introduced.name: Parameters as functions of chunks
concepts_introduced.definition: Optional simplification making $\alpha, \theta, \eta$ constant per chunk, turning the momentum recurrence into an LTI system computable by global convolution; not used in experiments.

concepts_introduced.name: Deep memory
concepts_introduced.definition: Memory MLP with $L_{\mathcal{M}} \ge 2$ layers; strictly more expressive than matrix (linear-regression) memory; empirically better perplexity at long lengths at a linear throughput cost.

assumptions_and_scope: Scale is modest and explicitly provisional: 170M/340M/400M/760M parameters, 15-30B training tokens, 4K training context; a v1 footnote states larger-model results are being finalized for a future version. Several implementation-critical details are unspecified in v1: the exact parameterization of the gates $\alpha_t, \theta_t, \eta_t$ (functional form, initialization), the memory MLP width/activation, how the momentum buffer is handled across chunk boundaries during training vs decoding, number of memory heads (if any), the chunk size $b$ and MAC segment size $C$ used, and how $\mathcal{M}_0$ is set (learned vs zero). Theorem 4.1 (beyond-$TC^0$) is stated without an included proof. The chunkwise scheme is an APPROXIMATION of the pure online update (gradients within a chunk are 'stale', taken at chunk-start weights); the paper does not quantify the approximation's effect or the sensitivity to $b$. Eq. 17 is written with $x$ in place of $(\mathbf{k}, \mathbf{v})$ — shorthand that a re-implementer must undo. The MAC write step $\mathcal{M}_t = \mathcal{M}_{t-1}(y_t)$ leaves the within-segment write granularity implicit. Baseline numbers for 400M models are reused from the Gated DeltaNet paper rather than re-run; BABILong baseline numbers come from the benchmark authors. Code was 'to be released soon' (PyTorch and JAX) but is not available with v1, and the throughput comparison concedes the LMM lacks the fused-kernel maturity of Mamba2. Scope of evidence spans language modeling, commonsense reasoning, S-NIAH/BABILong retrieval-reasoning, time-series forecasting (memory module dropped into the Simba framework), and DNA classification — but the >2M-context claim rests on BABILong (MAC, fine-tuned setting).
experiments_and_scale: Setup: 170M/340M/400M on 15B FineWeb-Edu tokens, 760M on 30B; Llama-2 tokenizer, 4K train length, AdamW 4e-4 cosine, 0.5M-token batches, wd 0.1 (Gated DeltaNet protocol). LANGUAGE MODELING + COMMONSENSE (Table 1; Wiki/LMB ppl, LMB/PIQA/HellaSwag/WinoGrande/ARC-e/ARC-c/SIQA/BoolQ acc): at every scale, standalone LMM beats all non-hybrid baselines (Transformer++, RetNet, GLA, Mamba, Mamba2, DeltaNet, TTT, Gated DeltaNet) — e.g., 340M: LMM avg 46.17 vs Gated DeltaNet 45.42, TTT 44.51; 760M: LMM Wiki ppl 20.04 / avg 51.56 vs Gated DeltaNet 21.18 / 49.69. Hybrids: MAC/MAG/MAL all beat Samba and Gated DeltaNet-H2; 760M MAG Wiki ppl 18.61, MAC avg 52.51 vs Gated DeltaNet-H2 19.88 / 51.49. MAC ≈ MAG > MAL consistently, indicting the standard sequential-hybrid (MAL) design itself. S-NIAH (RULER, 2K-16K; Table 2): LMM/variants stay 80-99% everywhere (MAC 98.4 on PK-16K, MAG 98.6 on N-16K) while Mamba2 collapses (PK-16K 5.4, W-8K/16K 0.0), DeltaNet degrades on N/W (no true erase), TTT sags at 16K (no forget gate) — a clean per-mechanism attribution: momentum+forgetting beats TTT, deep nonlinear memory + erasure beats Mamba2, forgetting beats DeltaNet. BABILONG (Fig. 6): few-shot, MAC outperforms Mamba-2.8B, RWKV-6-7B, RecurrentGemma-9B, Gemma-9B, Llama3.1-8B, GPT-4, GPT-4o-mini at a fraction of their parameters; fine-tuned, small MAC beats fine-tuned RMT/Mamba, Llama3.1-8B+RAG (~70x more params), and GPT-4/Qwen2.5-72B/Llama3.1-70B, sustaining accuracy beyond 2M tokens. MEMORY DEPTH (Fig. 7-8, Pile, 170M/360M/760M): deeper $L_{\mathcal{M}} = 2,3,4$ gives better perplexity and better length-robustness (largest gains at small scale) at a linearly lower training throughput; all depths scale linearly in sequence length. EFFICIENCY (Fig. 9): LMM slightly slower than Mamba2/Gated DeltaNet (deep memory + unoptimized kernel); MAL fastest of all (FlashAttention does the heavy lifting). TIME SERIES (Table 3, Simba backbone with LMM replacing Mamba): best MSE/MAE on ETTm1/m2/h1/h2, ECL, Traffic, Weather (e.g., ETTm1 0.358/0.387 vs PatchTST 0.387/0.400). DNA (Table 4, GenomicsBenchmarks): LMM competitive with HyenaDNA/Based/Mamba (e.g., Enhancer Cohn 75.2 best). ABLATIONS (Table 5): base LMM ppl 27.01 / reasoning 47.83 / long-context 92.68; removing weight decay is worst (ppl 29.04), then momentum (28.98), convolution (28.73), linear-instead-of-deep memory (28.49, long-context drops to 85.34), persistent memory (27.63); +Attn as MAC/MAG/MAL improves everything (MAC long-context 97.95).
systems_implications:
TRAINING PARALLELISM. The design is explicitly negotiated with hardware: the pure online rule is sequential, so the paper trades exactness for tensorization — per-chunk frozen-weight gradients turn the inner loop into batched matmuls ($\Theta_b \mathbf{B}_b (W_0 X - X) X^{\top}$-shaped), momentum becomes a length-$b$ input-dependent linear scan (same primitive as Mamba/S5 selective scan), and decay folds into cumulative products $\beta_i$. Only per-chunk $\Theta/\mathbf{B}$ diagonals are materialized. Nonlinearity is quarantined to chunk BOUNDARIES, so the sequential critical path is $N/b$ MLP-weight applications rather than $N$. The per-chunk-constant-gate option would further reduce the scan to an FFT-convolution (LTI), a knob for very-large-scale training that remains unexplored. Throughput is linear in context length (constant tokens/sec vs length, Fig. 8) and degrades linearly with memory depth — memory depth is a first-class cost axis that model configs must budget, like head count.

KERNELS. At publication the LMM had no fused kernel and still lands within striking distance of Mamba2/Gated DeltaNet throughput; the inner loop needs a fused chunk kernel doing (batched MLP fwd + bwd + scan + AXPY update) to close the gap. MAL's speed win is purely FlashAttention maturity — an important sociotechnical observation: composition choice (MAL vs MAC/MAG) trades measured-today throughput against quality, and the ranking may flip once LMM kernels mature. MAC's attention is block-diagonal over segments (Fig. 3a mask), i.e., FlashAttention over $C + N_p + N_l$-token windows — cost $O(N \cdot C)$ total, embarrassingly parallel across segments in prefill except for the memory's inter-segment dependency.

SERVING / STATE MATH. Recurrent state per sequence = memory weights + momentum buffer = $2 P_{\mathcal{M}}$ numbers per LMM (e.g., 2-layer, $d=1024$: ~4M values ≈ 8MB bf16), CONSTANT in context length, vs a KV cache of $2 N d$ per attention layer that at $N = 2M$, $d = 1024$ is ~8GB bf16 per layer — the entire >2M-context capability rests on this exchange. The momentum buffer doubles state vs a Gated-DeltaNet-style matrix state and must be carried across decode steps; naive multi-tenant batching needs per-request copies of the memory weights, making batched decode a batched-per-sample-weights (grouped GEMM / bmm) workload rather than shared-weight GEMM — the same serving pattern TTT imposes, but heavier because the state is a whole MLP. Prefill can ingest prompts chunk-parallel with the training-time formulation; decode is strictly sequential per token but O(1) per step. State checkpointing/eviction policy is learned, not managed (the $\alpha_t$ gate IS the eviction policy), which removes paged-KV machinery but makes memory behavior opaque to the runtime. Also note determinism/precision: the state is produced by an optimizer trajectory, so numerics (accumulation order, precision of the scan) can drift the 'cache' itself — a new consideration relative to KV caches. Test-time weight mutation also raises multi-tenant isolation and prompt-privacy considerations absent from frozen-weight serving.
connections: BACKWARD LINEAGE (this is the chronologically first paper of the six in this study set, so all its lineage is external). (1) Linear attention: Katharopoulos et al. 2020 kernelized attention into the recurrence $\mathcal{M}_t = \mathcal{M}_{t-1} + \mathbf{k}_t^{\top}\mathbf{v}_t$, $y_t = \mathbf{q}_t \mathcal{M}_t$ — Titans reads this as additive, overflow-prone Hebbian writing into a matrix memory. (2) Fast Weight Programmers (Schmidhuber 1992/1993; Schlag, Irie & Schmidhuber 2021 'linear transformers are secretly FWPs'): linear layers as writable key-value memory with Hebbian or delta learning rules — the paper positions the LMM as an FWP whose learning rule is upgraded from momentary-surprise Hebbian/delta to momentum + decay, and diagnoses ALL prior FWPs as missing token flow (no momentum) and mostly missing forgetting. (3) Delta rule line: Widrow-Hoff delta rule; DeltaNet (Yang, Wang, Zhang et al. 2024) parallelizing it over sequence length; Gated DeltaNet (Yang, Kautz, Hatamizadeh 2024) adding a forget gate — Appendix C proves LMM with linear memory and $\eta_t = 0$ IS Gated DeltaNet, so Titans is its strict generalization (momentum, depth, nonlinear inter-chunk recurrence). RWKV-7 is noted to share the same loss/formulation, hence also generalized. (4) Longhorn (Liu et al. 2024): same objective solved by implicit online learning (step $\delta_t = \theta_t/(1+\theta_t \mathbf{k}_t^{\top}\mathbf{k}_t)$), lacking a forget gate. (5) TTT (Sun et al. 2024): the direct predecessor — hidden state as a learner trained by mini-batch SGD, whose chunkwise 'gradients at batch-start weights' tensorization Titans builds on; Titans adds forgetting (weight decay), momentum, and an empirical case for deep memory, and Table 1/2 quantify each gap. (6) Mamba/Mamba2 and gated linear RNNs (GLA, Griffin, xLSTM, RetNet, LRU, S4/S5): supply the forgetting-gate concept (generalized here as weight decay), the associative-scan machinery, and the three-generation taxonomy of App. A (data-independent decay -> gated -> delta/online-learning rules), with LMM cast as the fourth generation (momentum/token-flow-aware). (7) Memory-augmented Transformers: RMT/segment-recurrent models — MAC is explicitly 'RMT with a neural network instead of a 16-dim memory vector'; persistent memory imports Sukhbaatar et al. 2019's attention-FFN unification and the attention-sink fix of StreamingLLM/LM-Infinite; Hymba inspires the parallel-heads reading of MAG. (8) Meta-learning: inner/outer-loop framing from learning-to-learn (Andrychowicz et al.), Reptile, CAVIA; test-time training's local-learning roots (Bottou & Vapnik). (9) Expressivity: Merrill et al.'s $TC^0$ ceiling for transformers/SSMs motivates Theorem 4.1. FORWARD, WITHIN THE SET: Titans supplies the vocabulary and the base recurrence that the later papers in this set (2504.13173, 2505.23735, 2511.07343, 2512.24695, 2606.03979) generalize — the memory-as-optimizer view (objective + retention + optimizer as design axes), deep memory, and the short-term/long-term/persistent decomposition; expect successors to attack its acknowledged gaps (better inner objectives beyond L2 regression, better inner optimizers beyond SGD+momentum, e.g., Muon-style, larger-scale validation, and self-referential/nested designs). WHAT IT LEAVES OPEN EXPLICITLY: replacing the MLP memory with architectures purpose-built for memorization (Memory Mosaics, Berges et al., Cetin et al. cited as candidates); the per-chunk-gate LTI simplification for large-scale training; scaling beyond 760M.
open_questions: (1) Approximation quality of the chunkwise inner loop: gradients within a chunk are evaluated at stale (chunk-start) weights — how does quality degrade with chunk size b, and does the train-time chunking match decode-time token-by-token updates (train/serve consistency)? The paper never ablates b. (2) Gate parameterization and stability: $\alpha_t, \theta_t, \eta_t$ are 'functions of the token' but their form, initialization, and the stability of an unconstrained learned optimizer trajectory over millions of steps are unspecified; nothing bounds $\|\mathcal{M}_t\|$ except learned decay. (3) Outer-loop memory cost: backprop through the unrolled inner loop over a 4K context requires storing per-chunk inner states/activations; the paper gives no activation-memory accounting or gradient-checkpointing recipe — a real concern for scaling context or memory depth at pre-training time. (4) Theorem 4.1 is asserted without proof in v1; the precise construction separating Titans from $TC^0$ is open to the reader. (5) Scale: all evidence is <=760M/30B tokens; whether momentum and deep memory retain their edge at 7B+ with optimized DeltaNet-family kernels is untested (the footnote promises larger models 'in the next version'). (6) Kernel gap: can a fused chunkwise LMM kernel reach Mamba2-class throughput, and does MAC/MAG then dominate MAL on both axes? (7) Serving semantics: per-request mutable weights raise batching (grouped-GEMM decode), state-snapshot/rollback (e.g., for speculative decoding or beam search — rolling back an optimizer trajectory is nontrivial), numerics-determinism, and privacy questions the paper does not touch. (8) MAC design constants: segment size C, N_p, and the write granularity of $\mathcal{M}_{t-1}(y_t)$ are unreported; the retrieval uses the PRE-update memory $\mathcal{M}^*_{t-1}$ — one-segment-stale reads whose effect is unmeasured. (9) Deep memory is only tested to $L_{\mathcal{M}} = 4$ as plain MLPs; the paper itself flags purpose-built memorization architectures as future work. (10) The per-chunk-constant-gate (LTI/global-convolution) fast path is proposed but never evaluated. FOR THE STUDY PAPER'S SCAFFOLDING LIST: readers from inference land will need primers on gradient/backprop mechanics (to parse 'surprise'), SGD momentum + weight decay as recurrences, bilevel meta-learning (inner vs outer loop, 'differentiating through an optimizer'), online regression/delta rule, associative scans, and $TC^0$/circuit-complexity claims.
